catalog.name: 2030 RES targets
catalog.description:
The achievement of the challenging goals for the development of renewable energy sources (RES) by 2030 as outlined in the PNIEC (National Integrated Energy and Climate Plan) and dictated by the REPowerEU program and the Fit for 55 package is mainly based on the contribution of solar and wind sources. The availability of areas suitable for hosting installations is a discriminating factor across different territorial realities and can highlight potential limitations to the development itself.

This section presents spatially based information that is framed within the energy territorial planning process and the monitoring of regional objectives assigned by the ministerial decree of June 21, 2024 (the so-called Suitable Areas Decree).
In addition to the goals and their degree of advancement, for each of the macro categories of plants considered in this section (photovoltaic, onshore wind, and offshore wind), the potential for territorial development is presented in terms of areas potentially available for new installations (estimate of eligible areas), as well as projects in the authorization phase (large plants).

It should be noted that the results of the eligible areas reported in the photovoltaic, onshore wind, and offshore wind sections are derived from RSE studies that are based on specific hypotheses and should be understood as purely indicative information regarding land availability.

members.name: Target and progress
members.description:
In order to align Italy with the latest EU objectives, the MASE, with the DM of June 21, 2024, has set an additional renewable energy power target of 80 GW to be achieved by the year 2030.
The Decree indicated both the contribution required from each Region and Autonomous Province, as well as the expected trajectories starting from the year 2021.

This collection includes the map of the regional renewable energy targets for 2030, as specified in the decree, and the map of their current level of achievement.

members.name: RES target by region
members.description:
Map of additional renewable energy power targets assigned to each Region and Autonomous Province by the Ministerial Decree of June 21, 2024.

Insights
The study conducted by RSE ( Scenarios to support the "Suitable Areas" decree) presents the methodologies and assumptions adopted for constructing scenarios for the distribution of the national target, which were then used to define regional targets.
The assignment of regional targets was based on the assumption that the entire increase in renewable energy power by 2030 is attributable solely to wind and photovoltaic sources.
However, this has no prescriptive effect and it remains up to the Regions and Autonomous Provinces to choose which technologies to focus on to achieve the target, according to the principle of "technological neutrality."

members.name: Regional progress toward the target
members.description:
The map shows the progress of each Region or Autonomous Province with respect to the target set by the Ministerial Decree of June 21, 2024. The data, expressed as a percentage, is calculated as the ratio between the sum of additional renewable energy capacity and the target.
All new renewable energy plants of any technology installed from 2021 onwards, net of decommissioning, contribute to the calculation of the additional capacity.

Data updated as of December 2023.

The data in absolute values is reported in the attributes.

members.name: Potential Photovoltaic
members.description:
This collection includes information on the extent of certain types of areas available for new photovoltaic installations (both ground-mounted and rooftop), as well as on the presence of proposed projects subject to Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA). These data are useful for assessing progress toward the 2030 renewable energy target.
The results shown in these maps are based on studies that rely on specific assumptions and should be understood as a guide for identifying areas potentially available for new photovoltaic installations. They provide planners with preliminary indications of the areas with the highest potential.

For further information on the estimation of these areas it is possible to consult the following document.

members.name: Potential Onshore wind
members.description:
This collection includes information on the extent of eligible areas for new onshore wind installations and on the presence of proposed projects subject to Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA). These data are useful for assessing progress toward the 2030 renewable energy target. The results shown in these maps are based on studies relying on specific assumptions and should be understood as a guide for identifying areas potentially available for new wind installations, providing planners with preliminary indications of the areas with the highest potential.

For further information on the estimation of these areas it is possible to consult the following document.

members.name: Areas available for onshore wind power installations
members.description:
This collection includes the map of available areas for new onshore wind power installations, obtained from areas with wind energy production at 100 m higher than 2250 MWh/MW and excluding urban areas and areas subject to environmental and cultural constrains.
The wind energy production map derives from the new anemological database provided by RSE and available from the Italian Wind Atlas AEOLIAN.

For further information on the estimation of these areas it is possible to consult the following document.

members.name: Potential Offshore wind
members.description:
This collection includes information on the extent of eligible areas for new offshore wind installations and on the presence of proposed projects subject to Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), useful for assessing progress toward the 2030 renewable energy target. The results shown in these maps are based on studies that rely on specific assumptions and represent preliminary indications of the areas with the highest potential, considering the current state of offshore technology.

For further information on the estimation of these areas it is possible to consult the following document.

members.name: Areas available for offshore wind power installations
members.description:
This collection provides an integrated overview of the Italian maritime space, useful for preliminary assessments of offshore wind development. It includes both Maritime Spatial Planning (MSP) information, derived from the official plans of the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport (MIT), and maps of areas potentially eligible for new offshore wind installations, broken down by distance from the coast, depth range, and producibility range.

The latter were identified by integrating the Mediterranean Sea bathymetry map, generated and released by the European Marine Observation and Data Network (EMODnet), with maps of theoretical annual specific producibility (calculated at an altitude of 150 m above sea level). The producibility maps are derived from the new Italian wind database produced by RSE and are available at AEOLIAN - Atlante EOLico ItaliANo.

For further information on the estimation of these areas it is possible to consult the following document.

members.name: Maritime spatial planning - simplified map
members.description:
The map shows the division of the sea into Planning Units (UP), each associated with one or more prevailing uses (priority, reserved, limited, or general), as defined by the Maritime Spatial Plans. The data come from the SID platform – Il portale del mare (https://www.sid.mit.gov.it/) and reflect the official designated uses identified by the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport (MIT), in accordance with European Directive 2014/89/EU.
To facilitate the interpretation of the map for offshore wind development purposes, the representation has been simplified by aggregating certain land-use classes. In particular, the areas have been reclassified according to the following criteria:

  • Areas with exclusive priority use for “energy”: primarily designated for energy production, with no competing uses.

  • Areas with non-exclusive priority use for “energy”: energy use is a priority, but it coexists with other priority uses.

  • Areas with generic use: no specific uses are identified, energy development therefore possible.

  • Areas with predominant use related to other priority uses: energy development is only possible if it does not interfere with the assigned priority uses.

  • Areas with limited or restricted use: energy development is not permitted.


This classification aims to provide a concise and functional overview of the planning context, in support of preliminary assessments for offshore wind development. The complete classification can be found in the “Sea uses” section of the “Territorial data” catalog.
